answer: Bonded collateral makes each identity costly to maintain, while correlated equivocation by \(k\) coordinated identities triggers pairwise penalties that scale as \(O(k^2)\), rather than linearly. Detection also applies asymmetric depreciation to exposed stake, compounding capital loss so a sybil swarm faces an exponential multiplier in losses. Such a swarm is no haven: its pearl of cheap identities becomes a vine of linked exposure.
